If sentiment is positive (≥0.67) in the last 3 days, increase forecast by 0.5–1.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to capture upward momentum.

If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) in the last 3 days, reduce forecast by 0.5–1.5% for early horizon (1–7 days) to avoid overestimating rebound.

If sentiment is neutral (0.33–0.67) and forecast is trending upward, apply a 1–2% downward correction in mid horizon (8–15 days) to prevent overfitting to recent highs.

If sentiment is neutral and forecast is trending downward, apply a 1–2% upward correction in mid horizon (8–15 days) to counteract pessimism bias.

In late horizon (16–30 days), if sentiment is positive and forecast is above 70, reduce by 0.5–1.0% to avoid overextension; if negative and below 68, increase by 0.5–1.0% to avoid underestimating reversal.

If sentiment swings from negative to positive within 3 days, apply a 1–2% upward correction to the forecast starting from day 5 onward to capture sentiment reversal momentum.
